objective: Replace the R5 pre-registration's hand-chosen per-case hurt cap of +0.010 with a cap derived from the training split's own leave-one-out spread at a stated confidence level, record the derivation as a reusable threshold, and re-run the R5 GO/NO-GO against the derived cap without making a scoring call
rationale: The priority review closed on 2026-08-05 with element 4 verified as PRIOR-EXISTS in concept and NO-PRIOR-FOUND as a turbulence-closure instance. The concept's canonical statement is Thomas, Theocharous and Ghavamzadeh, High Confidence Policy Improvement, Proceedings of the 32nd ICML, PMLR 37, pages 2380 to 2388, 2015, abstract read verbatim from the PMLR record this session: the user may select any performance lower-bound and confidence level and the algorithm guarantees the probability of returning a policy below that bound is at most the stated confidence level. The same discipline appears in clinical trials as a non-inferiority margin pre-specified in the protocol so it cannot be chosen after the data. Our R5 gate has the pre-specification half and not the derivation half. The R5-alpha05 regime pre-registration, section 3, declares the cap before any leave-one-out delta exists, which is what protects against leakage, but it never says why 0.010, and the verdict turned on that number alone: variant B failed rule three at plus 0.0167 on alpha_05_4071_3036 while passing rules one and two. A cap that decides a NO-GO and cannot say where it came from is a constant in workflow code, which the innovation standard's stage 3 sends to the physics-rules registry as a number with a derivation. This is the literature charter's section 6 trigger 2 and the reading does not close without it. Prediction, written before the run: the derived cap will land above 0.010, because the training split's leave-one-out deltas already range to better than minus 0.035 and a spread-based bound at any conventional confidence level is wider than a round number chosen by eye, so the honest outcome may be that R5 passes a defensible cap where it failed an arbitrary one. That outcome must not be taken as authorising a scoring call by itself, because the cap is being redefined after its own verdict is known and that ordering is exactly what the R5 document's own section 6 refuses.
gate: The cap is derived from train-only quantities at a stated confidence level, with the derivation written down before it is evaluated, and the derived value is recorded in a standards file rather than a script constant. The re-run reports the R5 GO/NO-GO under both the old and the new cap side by side, and states plainly that the new cap was fixed after the old verdict was known and therefore cannot on its own authorise the round-5 scoring call. Zero scoring calls, zero test-case file opens, in-sample gate PASS before and after
cost_basis: measured: the R5 training and leave-one-out run cost 62 s wall at a 2-core cap, about 2 core-min, recorded in the R5-alpha05 regime pre-registration. This item re-uses those already-computed leave-one-out deltas for the derivation and re-runs the selection arithmetic, so the compute is the same run at most once more plus seconds of arithmetic
expected_knowledge_gain: Either outcome pays. A derived cap that R5 still fails converts a hand-chosen NO-GO into a defensible one and strengthens the pre-registration section of both the submission draft and the LaTeX report, where the R5 no-go is currently the sole evidence that the discipline binds. A derived cap that R5 passes exposes that the entry of record was held at 0.0654 by an arbitrary constant, which is a finding about our own method rather than about the benchmark, and it produces the second-stage pre-registration that section 6 of the R5 document already names as the successor candidate. Either way the lab gains one threshold with a stated derivation, reusable by any future gate, and a citation of the established form of the rule where it currently has none
